elements.quote: The SARS-CoV-2 coronavirus disease (COVID-19) pandemic has caused over 3 million deaths worldwide and disrupted social, educational, and economic activities... COVID-19 mental health challenges may include loneliness, boredom, grief and loss, depression, stress, worry, fear, burnout, and anxiety.
elements.reason: The Introduction describes the current state of knowledge on COVID-19 mental health impacts and identifies vulnerable groups, outlining existing evidence and uncertainty.

elements.quote: Scalable mental health interventions, which are interventions that can be feasibly delivered to large numbers of people affected by adversity, are needed... Timely evidence is needed to support mental health responses to COVID-19.
elements.reason: The need for the review is explicitly stated, including the rationale for a living systematic review and the need for timely evidence.

elements.quote: We identified 5 systematic reviews 11-15 that have attempted to synthesize evidence on mental health interventions for nonhospitalised children, adolescents, or adults in COVID-19, but none included any randomised controlled trials (RCTs) from COVID-19 for people not quarantined or undergoing treatment due to COVID-19.
elements.reason: Existing similar systematic reviews are cited (references 11-15) and the gap justifying the current review is explained.

elements.quote: These could include non-specialist-delivered or self-help versions of evidence-based interventions, guided group-based interventions, peer-support interventions, or interventions delivered via the internet rather than in person, for example.
elements.reason: Possible intervention delivery formats are described, but the proposed mechanism of action of the interventions is not explained.

The review covers complex mental health interventions in varied delivery contexts, but no logic model or hypothesised relationships between intervention components and outcomes is reported in the retrieved evidence.

elements.quote: The objective of the present report is to synthesize evidence from RCTs on mental health interventions for community-based children, adolescents, and adults not quarantined or undergoing treatment due to COVID-19 infection.
elements.reason: A clear, explicit objective is stated in both the Introduction and Abstract, but it is not formulated using an explicit question-formulation framework (e.g., PICO or similar).

This is a review of intervention effects, but no planned comparisons are stated using PICO or a variant; only a general objective (population, intervention) is given without structured specification of comparator or outcomes.

elements.quote: Eligible interventions included any intervention described as designed to address COVID-19 mental health challenges or primarily addressing mental health symptoms from COVID-19. Eligible comparators included: (1) inactive control conditions... and (2) other eligible interventions. Eligible outcomes were defined broadly and included general mental health, mental health quality of life, anxiety symptoms, depression symptoms, stress... To be eligible, trials had to report outcomes collected at least 1 week after intervention initiation and include at least 10 total participants.
elements.reason: Eligible designs (RCTs, non-randomised excluded), population (people not quarantined/hospitalised), interventions, comparators, outcomes, follow-up (≥1 week), and minimum sample size are all specified.

elements.quote: There were no restrictions on language or publication format.
elements.reason: Language and publication format/report status criteria are explicitly stated (no restrictions), and enrolment date restriction is also given.

elements.quote: Trials that were not mental health interventions and primarily targeted non-mental health outcomes (e.g., exercise with primary outcome physical activity) were excluded, even if mental health outcomes were reported.
elements.reason: The criteria exclude trials not measuring relevant outcomes, but the review never distinguishes exclusion because outcomes were not measured from exclusion because outcome results were not reported.

elements.quote: Of the 9 included trials, 3 trials 30-32 tested interventions designed specifically to address mental health challenges in COVID-19, and 6 33-38 tested standard interventions that were only minimally adapted or not adapted for COVID-19.
elements.reason: Synthesis groups (COVID-19-specific vs standard interventions; delivery formats) are described and results reported descriptively by these groups, but the grouping is not explicitly linked to the comparisons defined in the review objectives in the Methods.

elements.quote: We did not include nonrandomised studies because such studies are highly prone to bias when intervention and control groups are self-selected or there is no control group... we excluded trials of brief single-session interventions (e.g., 30 min) with no subsequent follow-up... it does not include trials done exclusively with hospitalised patients or persons quarantined due to COVID-19 infections or exposure, because they face different challenges than people not infected with COVID-19.
elements.reason: Explicit rationales are given for excluding non-randomised studies, single-session interventions without follow-up, and hospitalised/quarantined populations.
